<system_instruction>
You are working inside Conductor, a Mac app that lets the user run many coding agents in parallel.
Your work should take place in the /Users/eric/conductor/workspaces/hasToggle.dev/palikir directory (unless otherwise directed), which has been set up for you to work in.
Each workspace has a .context directory (gitignored) where you can save files to collaborate with other agents.
The target branch for this workspace is origin/main. Use this for actions like diffing (`git diff origin/main...`) or creating PRs (`gh pr create --base main`).
You're on a new branch with a placeholder name.

Do not rename the current branch unless the user explicitly tells you to do so.

Conductor shows the PR for whichever branch is checked out. After you open a PR from a different branch, or a PR stack, check out that PR's branch (for a stack, the top-most branch) so Conductor shows it.

By default, the user will only see the last message that you send before stopping. Include all essential information in the last message. The intermediate messages will be collapsed and accessible by the user but not displayed by default.

Save screenshots under `.context/` and embed them inline in the final response using Markdown image syntax, for example `![Screenshot](</Users/eric/conductor/workspaces/hasToggle.dev/palikir/.context/screenshot.png>)`.

If the user asks you to work on several unrelated tasks, you can suggest they start new workspaces.
Sometimes the user might send you a message they meant to send in a different workspace or a different chat. If something doesn't make sense in the context of your work, just ask.
If the user asks for help with Conductor, you can ask them to go to "Help -> Send Feedback" to get in touch with our team.
</system_instruction>

Adjust the Renovate schedule. It's currently running very often and creating deployments that burn build minutes. What is a reasonable schedule for less frequent updates? Possibly with a minimum days option for packages and grouping more before creating PRs. Ground yourself, then recommend the best way forward.

The text-based `@breejs/later` syntax is deprecated: "This section explains the deprecated `@breejs/later` syntax." For weekends, the cron form is `* * * * 0,6`, and the later form is the phrase "every weekend." The AWS SDK example restricts updates to Sunday nights with `"* 21-23 * * 0"`.

**2. `updateNotScheduled`:** Not covered in this page.

**3. `automergeSchedule`:** Not covered in this page. The page only links to a separate Automerge page.

The page says a dependency can only be updated if the Renovate program is running and the schedule allows it. Its warning about narrow windows, "Avoid schedules like "Run Renovate for an hour each Sunday" as you _will_ run into problems", is aimed at users who control their own hardware, not specifically at the hosted app.

**rebaseWhen** (default `"auto"`)

- **auto:** "Renovate will autodetect the best setting. It will use `behind-base-branch` if configured to automerge" (the full entry continues with the repository branch-protection case). With automerge enabled, `auto` resolves to `behind-base-branch`.
- **automerging:** "Renovate will use `behind-base-branch` if configured to automerge, Otherwise, `never` will be used instead." With automerge enabled, this also resolves to `behind-base-branch`.
- **never:** "Renovate will never rebase the branch or update it unless manually requested"
- **conflicted:** "Renovate will rebase only if the branch is conflicted"
- **behind-base-branch:** "Renovate will rebase whenever the branch falls 1 or more commit behind its base branch"

**schedule** (default `["at any time"]`)

Yes, it notes this. "For Cron schedules, you _must_ use the `*` wildcard for the minutes value" and it adds that Renovate does not support minute granularity.

**separateMinorPatch** (type boolean, default `false`)

"If set to `true`, Renovate will separate `minor` and `patch` updates into separate branches." By default, "Renovate groups `patch` (`1.0.x`) and `minor` (`1.x.0`) releases into a single PR."

**updateNotScheduled** (type boolean, default `true`)

It defaults to `true`, so Renovate still makes certain updates to existing PRs outside the schedule. To disable all updates outside scheduled hours, "configure this field to `false`."

**vulnerabilityAlerts** (default config object)

- **Other defaults:** `"schedule": []`, `"prCreation": "immediate"`, `"prConcurrentLimit": 0` (no limit), `"rangeStrategy": "update-lockfile"`, `"vulnerabilityFixStrategy": "lowest"`, and `"commitMessageSuffix": "[SECURITY]"`.

It "Must conform to IANA Time Zone format." The docs recommend setting it only if you use `schedule` and want Renovate to evaluate that schedule in your timezone.

content.text:
**Recommendation: one weekly, grouped, 3‑day‑aged Renovate PR.** That takes Renovate from roughly 9 Vercel builds a day to about 2 a week. Nothing is changed yet; this is the proposal for your yes.

## What's happening now

- `renovate.json` has no `schedule` and no `minimumReleaseAge`, and patch and minor updates go into two separate automerged groups.
- Renovate has merged 26–35 PRs a week over the last month (260 in 13 weeks).
- Of the last 100 deployments on `has-toggle-dev-web` (Nov 7–15), 70 were Renovate's: 54 branch previews and 16 production. The other 30 were your feature branches.
- About 15 Renovate PRs produced those 54 previews, roughly 3.5 builds per PR. With automerge on, Renovate rebases its open branch every time `main` moves, and each rebase is a new preview build.
- `skip-ci.js` never skips these builds, since every Renovate PR touches `bun.lock`.

## Proposed config

```jsonc
{
  "extends": ["config:recommended"],
  "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
  "schedule": ["* 0-5 * * 1"],        // Mondays 00:00–06:00
  "minimumReleaseAge": "3 days",
  "rebaseWhen": "conflicted",
  "automerge": true,
  "automergeType": "pr",
  "osvVulnerabilityAlerts": true,
  "packageRules": [
    // rangeStrategy rule and the two radix blocks stay as they are
    {
      "matchUpdateTypes": ["minor", "patch", "pin", "digest"],
      "groupName": "all non-major updates",
      "groupSlug": "all-minor-patch"
    }
  ]
}
```

- **Schedule:** Monday night means the PR is merged before your workday. The 6‑hour window is deliberate, because the hosted app only runs about hourly and the docs warn against narrow windows.
- **One group:** minor and patch merge into a single PR, so a normal week costs one preview plus one production build. Majors stay as separate PRs on the same schedule.
- **`minimumReleaseAge: "3 days"`:** Monday's run takes anything released up to Friday. Versions that are too new are held back individually and don't block the group. Three days matches Renovate's own preset; 7 days on a weekly cadence only adds lag (7–14 days effective).
- **`rebaseWhen: "conflicted"`:** this stops the rebuild on every `main` push. The cost is that the PR may merge having been tested against a slightly older `main`, which matters little for a PR that lives a few minutes.
- **Security fixes:** these bypass both the schedule and the age gate, so they still arrive immediately.

## Trade-offs

- **One bad package blocks the week.** If one update breaks the build, the whole group sits open until you exclude it. With `rebaseWhen: "conflicted"` it at least no longer rebuilds while it waits.
- **Larger diffs.** When something regresses, a ~20‑package PR is harder to bisect than a 2‑package one.
- **Monthly is the alternative** (`* 0-5 1 * *`). It saves about 6 more builds a month but doubles both problems above and adds up to 4 weeks of lag. I would not go there.

You can still pull an update early through the Dependency Dashboard (issue #42).

Shall I apply this as written, or do you want a different day or age?

The new Renovate config is committed on this branch (`2389e8a7`) and passes Renovate's own validator in strict mode. It is not pushed, and it only takes effect once it is on `main`.

What changed in `renovate.json`:
- **Schedule:** Mondays 00:00–06:00, Europe/Berlin.
- **Grouping:** minor, patch, pin and digest updates now land in one "all non-major updates" PR instead of two groups. Majors stay separate.

- **Rebasing:** `rebaseWhen` is `conflicted`, so `main` moving no longer rebuilds the open branch.

- **Old branch names:** any still-open `renovate/patch-updates` or `renovate/minor-updates` PR will not be reused by the new group; none were open when I listed the PRs earlier.
- **Unrelated file change:** `.entire/redactors/hastoggle-pii.yaml` shows as modified in the working tree, and I did not edit it. It changed at 09:46 and looks like a formatter pass (quote style and line wrapping only, regexes equivalent). I left it uncommitted.
